l1: Is the issue related to sleep, hibernate, shutdown, Fast Startup, or battery drain?
Does the device use S3 Sleep or S0 Modern Standby, and does it happen on AC, battery, or both?
Is this a physical PC, laptop, or a virtual machine — VM power behaves very differently?
When did the power behavior begin, and did it follow an update, driver change, or BIOS update?
Has the user or IT team already run 'powercfg /energy' or 'powercfg /batteryreport', and if so, what did it show?
Does the symptom happen consistently, or only under specific conditions (docked vs undocked, specific app running, time of day)?
l2: What power plan is active — Balanced, High Performance, Power Saver, or a custom/Ultimate Performance plan?
Are power settings enforced via Group Policy (Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Power Management) or an Intune Settings Catalog profile?
Is 'Allow wake timers' enabled or disabled for this device's intended use case?
If this is a VM, is the hypervisor's own power management (Hyper-V Save State, Azure auto-shutdown) being confused with in-guest Windows sleep?
Is this device part of a pilot group for a new GPO/Intune power policy, or already broadly deployed?

l1: Run 'powercfg /a' to list available sleep states on the device.
Run 'powercfg /batteryreport /output C:\battery.html' to generate a battery health report comparing Design Capacity to Full Charge Capacity.
Run 'powercfg /energy /output C:\energy.html' for a full energy efficiency and problem-device audit.
Confirm the current power plan with 'powercfg /getactivescheme'.
l2: Run 'powercfg /requests' to identify exactly what process, service, or driver is blocking sleep or the display timeout.
Run 'powercfg /lastwake' to identify what woke the device from its last sleep cycle.
Run 'powercfg /devicequery wake_armed' and 'powercfg /devicequery wake_from_any' to see which devices, including Wake-on-LAN NICs, can wake the PC.
Check 'HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power' (HibernateEnabled) to confirm hibernate/Fast Startup configuration state.

l1: Reset the power plan to the default Balanced scheme with 'powercfg -restoredefaultschemes'.
Disable Fast Startup with 'powercfg /h off' (or via Control Panel) if update or shutdown-state issues are suspected.
For a wake device conflict, uncheck 'Allow this device to wake the computer' under Device Manager > Power Management for that device.
Confirm 'Turn off display' and 'Sleep after' timeouts are not set to Never when the device is expected to sleep.
If USB peripherals randomly disconnect, check Device Manager > that device > Power Management for 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' and uncheck it for affected devices.
For servers/workstations that should never sleep, apply the High Performance (or Ultimate Performance where available) plan rather than leaving Balanced defaults in place.
l2: If wake timers are the cause, disable them per-plan via 'powercfg -waketimers' and, in a managed environment, through the 'Allow wake timers' GPO or CSP.

If Group Policy is silently overriding local settings, check Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Power Management — a GPO-enforced value always wins and greys out the local UI option.
For Intune-managed devices, check the Settings Catalog 'Power' profile, or a Custom OMA-URI under './Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/Power/', for a conflicting assignment.

On a VM, do not troubleshoot Windows sleep/hibernate directly — S3 sleep is typically unsupported; use the hypervisor's Save State/Pause or an Azure auto-shutdown schedule instead, and always run Sysprep with '/Mode:VM' on VM-based reference images.

l1: Attach the battery report generated by 'powercfg /batteryreport'.
Record the exact symptom — won't sleep, wakes randomly, battery drains fast, or updates won't apply after shutdown.
Note the current power plan and whether it is GPO/Intune-enforced or user-configurable.
Confirm whether the device is physical or virtual.
l2: Collect 'powercfg /energy' output for driver and setting inefficiencies.
Collect 'powercfg /requests' and 'powercfg /lastwake' output captured at the time of the issue.
Export the Event Viewer System log filtered on Source: Power-Troubleshooter.
Record the applicable GPO or Intune power policy path and its configured values for comparison against local settings.

device_wont_sleep_or_wakes_unexpectedly.title: Device won't sleep, or wakes unexpectedly on its own

steps.action: Run 'powercfg /requests' to see what is currently blocking sleep
steps.expect: Lists the specific process, driver, or service holding a power request

steps.action: If the device already slept and woke unexpectedly, run 'powercfg /lastwake' instead
steps.expect: Names the specific device or timer that caused the wake

steps.action: Cross-check the named device/process against 'powercfg /devicequery wake_armed'
steps.expect: Confirms whether that device is explicitly allowed to wake or block sleep

steps.action: In Device Manager > that device > Power Management, uncheck 'Allow this device to wake the computer'
steps.expect: Device is removed from the wake-armed list

steps.action: If a scheduled task or Windows Update wake timer is the cause, disable wake timers via 'powercfg -waketimers' or GPO
steps.expect: Wake timer no longer fires outside of maintenance windows

steps.action: Put the device to sleep and monitor for the previous behavior
steps.expect: Device sleeps normally and does not wake unexpectedly

steps.action: Run 'powercfg /batteryreport /output C:\battery.html' and open the report
steps.expect: Report generates showing Design Capacity vs Full Charge Capacity

steps.action: Compare Full Charge Capacity against Design Capacity
steps.expect: A drop below roughly 70% of design capacity indicates a worn battery rather than a settings issue

steps.action: If capacity looks healthy, run 'powercfg /energy' and check Task Manager > Performance > Energy Usage
steps.expect: Identifies a specific background app or inefficient driver driving the drain

steps.action: If battery health is below ~70% of design capacity, arrange a battery replacement
steps.expect: New battery restores expected runtime

steps.action: If a background app is the cause, close or update it, and confirm the power plan is Balanced or Power Saver on battery, not High Performance
steps.expect: Energy usage drops back to expected levels

steps.action: Re-run the battery report after a full charge/discharge cycle
steps.expect: Runtime matches expectations for the device's battery health

sleep_missing_from_start_menu.title: Sleep option is missing from the Start menu power controls

steps.action: Run 'powercfg /availablesleepstates'
steps.expect: Shows whether S3 sleep is listed as available or unsupported on this hardware

steps.action: If S3 is not listed, check the device's BIOS/UEFI for an S3 support setting
steps.expect: Confirms whether S3 is disabled in firmware or genuinely unsupported (common on S0 Modern Standby hardware)

steps.action: Enable S3 in BIOS/UEFI if present, or run 'powercfg /hibernate on' which sometimes restores the Sleep entry
steps.expect: Sleep option reappears in the Start menu power controls

steps.action: Re-check the Start menu power options
steps.expect: Sleep is listed and functions correctly

updates_not_applying_after_shutdown.title: Windows Updates don't finish applying after Shut Down

steps.action: Confirm Fast Startup is enabled (Control Panel > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do)
steps.expect: Fast Startup checkbox is enabled, explaining the incomplete update behavior

steps.action: Confirm the user was using Shut Down rather than Restart to apply the update
steps.expect: Fast Startup only saves the kernel on Shut Down; Restart always does a full cold boot

steps.action: Instruct the user to always use Restart (not Shut Down) when applying updates
steps.expect: Updates that require a full cold boot complete correctly

steps.action: Optionally disable Fast Startup entirely with 'powercfg /h off'
steps.expect: Every shutdown becomes a full cold boot, avoiding the issue going forward

steps.action: Re-check Windows Update history after the next Restart
steps.expect: Update shows as successfully installed with no repeat pending state

vm_power_settings_misapplied.title: Windows sleep/hibernate settings behave unexpectedly inside a VM

steps.action: Confirm the affected machine is a virtual machine (Hyper-V, VMware, or Azure), not physical hardware
steps.expect: Confirms VM context, since S3 sleep and battery reporting behave differently in guests

steps.action: Check whether the guest OS's power plan or hibernate settings are being applied at all, given most hypervisors don't support in-guest S3/S4
steps.expect: Confirms whether the guest setting is simply a no-op under this hypervisor

steps.action: Switch to the hypervisor's own power controls (Hyper-V Save State, VMware Suspend, or an Azure auto-shutdown schedule) instead of in-guest sleep/hibernate
steps.expect: VM pauses/resumes correctly using supported hypervisor mechanisms

steps.action: If this VM was built as sysprepped template, confirm Sysprep was run with '/Mode:VM' to skip irrelevant physical-hardware detection
steps.expect: Template generalizes cleanly without hardware-detection delays

steps.action: Re-test the intended pause/resume behavior using the hypervisor's controls
steps.expect: VM behaves as expected for the intended use case

usb_devices_disconnect_randomly_selectiv.title: USB peripherals randomly disconnect due to selective suspend

steps.action: Confirm the disconnects correlate with idle periods rather than being constant/immediate
steps.expect: Confirms a power-saving suspend behavior rather than a hardware fault

steps.action: Check Device Manager > Universal Serial Bus controllers > each Root Hub's Power Management tab for 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'
steps.expect: Identifies which hub/device has selective suspend enabled

steps.action: Uncheck the power-saving option for the affected hub/device, or disable USB selective suspend fleet-wide via the advanced power plan settings
steps.expect: Devices stop disconnecting under idle conditions

steps.action: Leave the peripheral idle for the previous disconnect interval and confirm it stays connected
steps.expect: No further random disconnects

cpu_throttled_unexpectedly_min_max_state.title: CPU seems throttled/slow even under load on AC power

steps.action: Check Task Manager > Performance > CPU for the current clock speed under load versus the rated base/boost speed
steps.expect: Confirms the CPU is actually running below expected speed

steps.action: Check the active power plan's Minimum/Maximum processor state settings via 'powercfg /q'
steps.expect: Identifies whether Maximum processor state is capped below 100%

steps.action: Set Maximum processor state back to 100% for the AC power plan (or switch to High Performance)
steps.expect: CPU is permitted to run at full rated speed

steps.action: Re-check Task Manager under load
steps.expect: CPU reaches expected clock speeds
